From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-18T10:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Spike in gen latency + 502s across checkout pipeline

Laura / Monica —

Preliminary: we see a spike in tail token latency on the Dedicated GPU pool serving neptune-prod between 08:43–09:05 UTC. Key signals:
- 99.9th percentile token latency rose ~6x versus baseline, correlating with a sudden increase in long-context requests for their checkout route.
- Autoscaler did not add capacity quickly enough due to a transient metric gap (delay in aggregated pod CPU signal) — this exposed a KV cache eviction pattern causing increased memory pressure.
- A recently enabled aggressive batching optimization (deployed 07/15) has a poorly-handled backpressure case when many long-sequence requests arrive concurrently; the batching logic increased queue times then timed out, yielding 502s.

Attachments: neptune_incident_rtc_logs.zip (trimmed), service_timeline_20260718.csv

Short-term mitigation proposed (TL;DR):
1) rollback the batching tweak for Dedicated pools serving long-context routes (owner: infra; ETA 2h)
2) enable stricter per-tenant request size caps for the checkout route (owner: product-engineering; ETA 4h)
3) provide a one-time capacity bump for Neptune while we validate (ops; ETA 1h)

I’ll draft an RCA doc and timeline.

—Markus
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Team —

I need this by 12:30 UTC so I can brief our Head of Sales and Legal for any credit discussions.

Thanks — we’re on a tight timeline here.

—Laura
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-18T16:42:00Z
Subject: RE: Neptune Logistics incident — RCA & corrective actions (v1)

Team — attaching the RCA and the corrective action tracker (neptune_rca_v1.pdf). Summary below for exec distribution:

What happened (brief):
- A recent batching optimization mis-handled concurrent long-sequence requests, increasing per-request queue times and triggering timeouts (502s). The autoscaler visibility laged due to a metrics aggregation delay, so capacity did not ramp fast enough. The combination produced higher tail token latency and HTTP 5xx at user-facing endpoints.

Customer impact:
- 22 minutes of degraded service during morning peak; ~30% of checkout calls returned 502s; estimated lost orders ~80 (customer reported).

Immediate corrective actions (owner — ETA):
- Rollback batching tweak on Dedicated pools (markus_klein — completed 07/18 11:03 UTC)
- Emergency capacity bump for Neptune pool (ops team — completed 07/18 11:20 UTC)
- Per-tenant request size cap enforced for checkout route (product-engineering — completed 07/18 12:15 UTC)

Medium-term fixes (owner — ETA):
- Add conservative backpressure safeguards to batching logic + unit/integration tests (markus_klein — ETA 2026-08-05)
- Improve autoscaler signal redundancy to avoid single-metric dependency (platform infra — ETA 2026-08-12)
- Customer-facing runbook for order-of-magnitude traffic bursts and recommended request size limits (solutions — ETA 2026-08-01)

Follow-through tracker: owners assigned and weekly check-ins scheduled; I’ll maintain a public tracker (link below) and own customer comms until Neptune signs off on the plan.

Attachments: neptune_rca_v1.pdf, service_timeline_20260718.csv

—Monica
Head of Customer Reliability
